research_rationale: Executive Order 12597 of May 13, 1987 (52 FR 18335, Federal Register Vol. 52 No. 94, Friday May 15, 1987) establishes procedures for presidential review of Department of Transportation international aviation decisions under Section 801 of the Federal Aviation Act. The U.S. Code search over release point 119-121 returned the order printed in full as a note to 49 U.S.C. 41307; that is a machine lead whose archive bytes are not held, so the current predicate cited for each clause is the held original clause text with the bounded searches (original-plus-bounded-search route). Searches: the Office of the Law Revision Counsel Code search, the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and the Federal Register catalogue disposition search were read for coverage notes before use. The only later-events hit for this order is the order revoking Executive Order 12547, which is its own section 1 and not a later event; no later order amends, revokes or supersedes Executive Order 12597 in the held sources. The order has no expiry, sunset or contingent end in its own text; the numbered day periods in sections 3 and 5 run per decision. The one gap noted is that the order names Executive Order 12356, which the packet holds only as actor context; no held source shows that fact ended any clause.

The deadlines in sections 3(b), 3(d) and 5(b) apply per decision and are not ends. No held source shows performance or extinguishment of any command.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12630 of March 15, 1988 (53 FR 8859, Federal Register Vol. 53 No. 53, Friday March 18, 1988; FR Doc. 88-6145) directs executive departments and agencies to evaluate the effect of their actions on constitutionally protected property rights. The held original is the machine-extracted text of the govinfo Federal Register PDF (pages 8859-8862) with title, Sections 1 to 6, the document number and the White House dateline present. Some printing runs are garbled by character recognition (for example in section 5(d) and 5(e)) but every section is present, so identity and completeness were confirmed against the text. The U.S. Code search over release point 119-121 returned the order printed as a note to 5 U.S.C. 601; that machine lead is not cited as a source because its archive bytes are not held, so the current predicate cited is the held original clause text with the bounded searches (original-plus-bounded-search route). Executive Order 13406 of 2006 section 4(c) says that order is to be implemented in a manner consistent with Executive Order 12630, and Executive Order 13061 of 1997 section 1(d) directs agencies to act in accordance with it; both recite the order without changing it. No held later order amends, revokes or supersedes it. The order has no expiry or contingent end of its own. The dates in section 1(c) and section 5(c) are 1988 deadlines for first performance and are not ends.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12657 of November 18, 1988 (53 FR 47513, Federal Register Vol. 53 No. 226, Wednesday November 23, 1988) directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (since 2003 the Department of Homeland Security) to assist emergency preparedness planning at commercial nuclear power plants when State or local governments decline or fail to prepare adequate plans. The held original is the machine-extracted text of the govinfo Federal Register PDF (pages 47513-47516) with title, preamble, sections 1 to 9 and the White House dateline present, so identity and completeness were confirmed against the text. The U.S. Code search over release point 119-121 returned the order printed as a note to 42 U.S.C. 5195, stated as amended by Executive Order 13286 section 41; that machine lead is not cited as a source because its archive bytes are not held. The held current CFR sections 44 CFR 352.3 and 352.28 cite the order, and the current predicate cited for other clauses is the held original clause text with the bounded searches (original-plus-bounded-search route). The only later amendment found in the held official texts is Executive Order 13286 section 41 (effective March 1, 2003), which replaced FEMA and its Director with the Department of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Homeland Security throughout sections 1(b) to 6; it is recorded as a later event on every clause containing those words. The packet chain also lists Executive Order 12977 as an amender, but the text of Executive Order 12977 (1995) does not amend this order; the item comes from a held source-ladder text of Executive Order 13286 mislabeled with that number, and the claim does not rely on it. No held source revokes or supersedes the order. Section 6(a) to (c) are implementation commands whose performance dates are not shown in held sources; they are carried as continuing on a disclosed limited basis, not as ended.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12793 of March 20, 1992 (57 FR 10281, Federal Register Vol. 57 No. 58, Wednesday March 25, 1992) continues the Presidential Service Certificate and the Presidential Service Badge. The held original is the machine-extracted text of the govinfo Federal Register PDF (PDF pages 11-16, which include neighbouring documents) in which the order appears from the title on page 10281 through section 5, the document marker and the White House dateline, so identity and completeness were confirmed against the text. The U.S. Code search over release point 119-121 returned the order printed as a note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 as amended by section 31 of Executive Order 13286 and section 1 of Executive Order 14131; that machine lead is not cited as a source because its archive bytes are not held, so the current predicate cited is the held original clause text with the bounded searches (original-plus-bounded-search route), and both amending orders are read from their held official texts. Later events were read from the held official Federal Register texts of both orders. Executive Order 13286 section 31 (effective March 1, 2003 by its section 92) replaced Transportation with Homeland Security in section 1. Executive Order 14131 section 1 (signed December 20, 2024) restated sections 1 and 2. Executive Order 13373 of 2005 amends Executive Order 11926 and only refers to section 1 of this order, so it is not a later event for this order. The order has no expiry or contingent end of its own. Sections 1 to 4 continue; section 5 (supersession of Executive Order 10879) was performed on signing.
savings_reason: The held text of the order contains no savings provision other than the supersession of Executive Order 10879 in section 5. The order is not ended, so no savings question arises for an ending.
earlier_end_check: Read the full held original and searched the held corpus for the order number (13 citing files). The held executive orders that name it are 13286 (section 31), 13373 (a reference only) and 14131 (sections 1 and 2); none revokes or supersedes the order. The only own-terms act is the supersession in section 5.
scope_check: All 5 inventory units were read against the held text. Sections 1 and 2 were amended by restatement and strike-and-insert; sections 3 and 4 are unchanged; section 5 is a performed supersession of an earlier order.
independent_command_check: The Certificate command (section 1), the Badge command (section 2) and the two limits in sections 3 and 4 are separate commands, each continuing. The supersession in section 5 is a one-time act independent of them.
savings_check: No savings clause is needed because the order remains in force.
